// diagnostic

E0135

A compile-time literal outside a range type's declared bounds

What

A compile-time literal outside a range type's declared bounds

Why

A range type only holds values inside its declared bounds, and this literal is outside them

Fix

Use a comptime integer within the range type's declared bounds.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0135: Tests/UI/LanguageFeatures/range_type_literal_proofs_cover_every_numeric_source_family.stderr.

Error [jet.LiteralOutsideRange]: `11` is outside `Severity`'s range 0..10
  --> Tests/UI/LanguageFeatures/range_type_literal_proofs_cover_every_numeric_source_family.jet:5:30
    |
  5 |     signed: Severity.from_i8(11)
    |                              ^^
 Why: A range type only holds values inside its bounds; `11` can never be a `Severity`
 Fix: Use a value in `0..10`, or widen the type's range
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0135

Error [jet.LiteralOutsideRange]: `12` is outside `Severity`'s range 0..10
  --> Tests/UI/LanguageFeatures/range_type_literal_proofs_cover_every_numeric_source_family.jet:6:32
    |
  6 |     unsigned: Severity.from_u8(12)
    |                                ^^
 Why: A range type only holds values inside its bounds; `12` can never be a `Severity`
 Fix: Use a value in `0..10`, or widen the type's range
